## Why This Is Asked
Tests the ability to implement secure access control with group-based SSH, key authentication, and per-group sudo without passwords. It covers account provisioning, SSH configuration, and basic hardening.

## Key Concepts
- Group-based SSH access (AllowGroups)
- Key-based authentication and disabling passwords
- Per-group sudoers (NOPASSWD)
- SSH service reload and verification

## Code Example
```bash
# create and assign
groupadd devs
useradd -m -G devs devadmin

# client side
ssh-keygen -t rsa -b 2048 -f id_rsa_devadmin -N ''
ssh-copy-id -i id_rsa_devadmin.pub devadmin@host

# server side (sshd_config)
AllowGroups devs
PasswordAuthentication no
PubkeyAuthentication yes
systemctl reload sshd

# sudoers
echo '%devs ALL=(ALL) NOPASSWD: ALL' > /etc/sudoers.d/devs
chmod 440 /etc/sudoers.d/devs
```

## Follow-up Questions
- How would you handle revoking access if a key is compromised?
- What logs would you inspect to verify SSH login attempts are from authorized keys?

## Why This Is Asked
This question evaluates practical system administration skills including systemd user services, timer configuration, file permissions, and log management in a real-world operational scenario.

## Key Concepts
- systemd user services and timers
- non-login user accounts and security
- basic Bash scripting for logging
- log rotation configuration with logrotate

## Code Example
```bash
# /home/usage/collect.sh
#!/bin/bash
hostname >> /var/log/usage.log
date '+%F %T' >> /var/log/usage.log
```

```ini
# /home/usage/.config/systemd/user/usage.service
[Unit]
Description=Log hostname and timestamp to usage.log

[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/home/usage/collect.sh
```

```ini
# /home/usage/.config/systemd/user/usage.timer
[Unit]
Description=Run usage logging every 15 minutes

[Timer]
OnCalendar=*:0/15
Persistent=true

[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
```

```bash
# /etc/logrotate.d/usage
/var/log/usage.log {
    daily
    rotate 7
    compress
    missingok
    notifempty
    create 644 usage usage
}
```
